svg.title: Maknae per-user isolation matrix
svg.desc: Lampson access-control matrix of which subject can read, carry or unwrap each user's model credential, prompt and turn metadata, with the enforcing control for each cell.
svg.text: Per-user isolation — the access-control matrix for model credentials
Rows are subjects, columns are objects; each cell is the right the code permits, keyed to its control, evidence and test below (ADR-0028).
A's key and B's key are standing objects, rated across all turns. The wrapping token, sealed blob, prompt and metadata are the objects of one of
A's turns; its metadata is the user, provider, model, conversation and key path.
The cli_b cells rest partly on OS uid separation between A's and B's processes, which no code in this repository proves.
Out of scope: root on the host and the Vault administrator, who can read everything.
sealed-only: carries it, cannot read it
unwrap-once: obtains it only by exchanging a single-use wrapping token, for one call
part: reads only the fields its footnote names
1. cli_a × key_a: A's own userpass identity reads it, response-wrapped (min_wrapping_ttl), and A can unwrap that token itself: the accepted residual
2. cli_a × key_b: Vault templated policy maknae-user scopes reads to maknae/users/{{identity.entity.aliases.<accessor>.name}}, so A's login reaches
only A's subtree — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:207 · docs/verification-walkthrough.md (C2, measured 403)
3. cli_a × wrap: Vault returns it to A's own wrapped read; a reply carrying the key instead is refused — bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:373 ·
4. cli_a × sealed: A's CLI seals it, so A already holds what it contains — bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:185 · crates/maknae-seal/src/seal.rs:54 · test:
5. cli_a × prompt: A writes it — bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:506
6. cli_a × meta: A chooses the providers.yaml entry; the CLI mints the conversation id — bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:519 · bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:553 ·
7. cli_b × key_a: Vault templated policy maknae-user scopes reads to maknae/users/{{identity.entity.aliases.<accessor>.name}}, so B's login cannot
read A's subtree, wrapped or not — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:207 · docs/verification-walkthrough.md (C2, measured 403)
8. cli_b × key_b: B's own userpass identity reads it, response-wrapped, and B can unwrap that token itself: the accepted residual #429, as for A —
9. cli_b × wrap: OS process isolation between uids, not proven by code here: the token sits unsealed in A's CLI memory between the wrapped read and
the seal, and B holding it could unwrap it at Vault directly; past the seal it travels only sealed, and the creation_path check only stops B using the
Egress Daemon with A's token — bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:373 · bins/maknae/src/agent.rs:185 · bins/maknae-egress/src/opener.rs:83 ·
10. cli_b × sealed: it crosses only A's plane connection; replayed in B's turn it does not open, because the AAD binds conversation and path and the
kernel derives the username from B's uid — crates/maknae-kernel/src/run.rs:862 · crates/maknae-kernel/src/provider_choice.rs:62 ·
11. cli_b × prompt: no control while A's CLI runs (#436, undecided): maknae agent takes the prompt as positional argv, and argv is world-readable on a
default host (Linux /proc/<pid>/cmdline without hidepid, macOS ps -ax -o args); the audit trail keeps only its digest and length, in a 0700 _maknae
12. cli_b × meta: part; no control while A's CLI runs (#436, undecided): argv is world-readable on a default host (Linux /proc without hidepid, macOS
ps), so B sees --provider <label> and the process owner; the audit trail holding the rest is written by maknaed in a 0700 _maknae directory —
13. agentd × key_a: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
14. agentd × key_b: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
15. agentd × wrap: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
16. agentd × sealed: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
17. agentd × prompt: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
18. agentd × meta: not built: no account, process or Vault identity exists yet (epic #420) — ADR-0028
19. kernel × key_a: maknaed's AppRole policy grants no KV path, and the wrapping token reaches it only sealed: the seal private key is held only by
the Egress Daemon (Linux root:root 0400 credential loaded by LoadCredentialEncrypted; macOS keychain ACL), and maknaed does not link maknae-seal;
residual: maknaed can attach a user's sealed token to content of its own choosing, using the key without reading it — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:138 ·
20. kernel × key_b: as for A's key: no KV grant in maknaed's AppRole policy, no seal private key, and maknae-seal is not linked; the same residual:
maknaed can attach B's sealed token to content of its own choosing — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:138 · packaging/common/maknae-egress.service ·
21. kernel × wrap: carried only inside the sealed blob; maknaed does not link maknae-seal and holds no seal private key —
22. kernel × sealed: forwarded as opaque bytes with the path it admitted; maknaed does not link maknae-seal and holds no seal private key —
23. kernel × prompt: prompt content transits maknaed on its way to the Egress Daemon: the open residual #417 — crates/maknae-kernel/src/run.rs:1561 ·
24. kernel × meta: maknaed decides on it: admission derives the username from the peer uid and composes the key path itself —
25. egress × key_a: creation_path and TTL checked before the unwrap; the key is held in a zeroizing buffer for one call, with no key cache —
26. egress × key_b: the same check on B's turns: the Egress Daemon sees each active user's key, one call at a time, so a compromised one harvests
every key used while it is compromised — crates/maknae-vault/src/wrap.rs:299 · ADR-0028 · test:
27. egress × wrap: opened only under this request's AAD, looked up (creation_path, TTL at most 60 s), then presented once to unwrap; Vault makes it
28. egress × sealed: it holds the seal private key and opens the blob only under this request's AAD — bins/maknae-egress/src/opener.rs:83 ·
29. egress × prompt: it builds the provider request from the turns — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:243 · test:
30. egress × meta: the egress frame carries the destination, model, admitted key path (naming the user), key field and conversation —
31. vault × key_a: Vault is the only store of a user's key, and hands it out only response-wrapped (min_wrapping_ttl) — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:209 ·
32. vault × key_b: Vault is the only store of a user's key, and hands it out only response-wrapped (min_wrapping_ttl) — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:209 ·
33. vault × wrap: Vault issues it; sys/wrapping/lookup is unauthenticated and reports its creation_path — crates/maknae-vault/src/api_request.rs:136 ·
34. vault × sealed: never sent to Vault: the client seals after its wrapped read, and the Egress Daemon presents the opened token, not the blob —
35. vault × prompt: no Vault request carries content: the wrapped read, lookup and unwrap carry only a token and a path —
36. vault × meta: part: it sees the user's userpass identity and the key path of the wrapped read, and the provider only as far as the key subpath
names it; never the model or conversation — deploy/vault-pki/main.tf:207 · crates/maknae-vault/src/api_request.rs:123
37. model × key_a: it receives the key as the bearer credential, which is inherent to an API key — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:258 · test:
38. model × key_b: on B's turns whenever B's chosen provider is this provider: no control keeps a user's key from their own provider —
39. model × wrap: never sent: the Egress Daemon sends only the opened key, as a bearer header — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:226 ·
40. model × sealed: never sent: the Egress Daemon opens it before the call and sends only the key — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:226 ·
41. model × prompt: it receives the conversation's turns, which is the point of the call — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:243 · test:
42. model × meta: part: the request names the model and its reasoning and output settings, never the user, conversation or key path, though the bearer
key identifies the user's account at the provider — crates/maknae-deputy/src/call.rs:243
Access-control matrix — B. W. Lampson, "Protection", 1971 (ACM SIGOPS OSR 8(1), 1974)
